methods.label: Compare the remaining distances
methods.explanation:
Imagine all three runners starting together. When \(A\) finishes, \(B\) has run \(d-20\) yards and \(C\) has run \(d-28\) yards. When \(B\) later finishes, \(C\) has run \(d-10\) yards.

During this last interval, \(B\) runs \(20\) yards while \(C\) runs
\[
(d-10)-(d-28)=18
\]
yards. Their speeds are constant, so whenever \(B\) runs \(20\) yards, \(C\) runs \(18\) yards and falls \(2\) yards farther behind.

Starting together, \(B\) must gain \(10\) yards by the end of the race. That requires five times this interval, so
\[
d=\frac{10}{2}\cdot20=100\text{ yards}.
\]
These conditions are consistent: speeds in the ratio \(A:B:C=100:80:72\) produce all three stated margins in a 100-yard race. The answer is choice C.
